ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r2.claim: The deniers habitually demand a sign of their own choosing and dismiss the signs already shown; the Qur’an answers that earlier scriptures had foretold it and that it is the enduring, greatest miracle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r2.anchor: هذه عادتهم في اقتراح الآيات كأنهم جعلوا ما ظهر من الآيات ليس بآيات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r3.claim: These readers use the feminine verb form matching the word sign; other readers use masculine agreement because the feminine noun is separated from the verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص تأتهم بالتاء على لفظ بينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r4.claim: The majority read proof in construct with what is in the earlier pages; a group reads it indefinite with tanwin and takes what as an appositive, with further case variants also reported.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بإضافة بينة إلى ما وفرقة منهم أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو بالتنوين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reads pages with a still ḥāʾ rather than the majority’s rounded vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور في الصحف بضم الحاء، وفرقة منهم ابن عباس بإسكانها

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر، نافع، أبو عمرو، يعقوب، حفص عن عاصم، قتيبة عن الكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r8.claim: These readers use the feminine تاء in أولم تأتهم; other named readers use يأتهم, treating البينة as masculine البيان and putting the verb first.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r8.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وحفص عن عاصم، وقتيبة عن الكسائي: أولم تأتهم بالتاء

ASAD-NOTES:20:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:intro/r2.claim: The surah's main theme is prophetic guidance and the shared truths of revealed religions, developed through Moses' story and the Qur'an's evidence in earlier scripture.
ASAD-NOTES:20:intro/r2.anchor: The main theme of Ta Ha is the guidance

ELMALILI:20:129-135/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:129-135/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:129-135/r3.claim: The Quran answers the demand for a sign by clearly explaining and proving the contents of the Torah, Gospel, and other revealed books, making Muhammad's prophethood manifest.
ELMALILI:20:129-135/r3.anchor: Tevrat ve İncil vesâir semâvî kitapların mündericâtını daha açık daha parlak bir surette beyan ve isbat eden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r8.claim: The verse says the Quran confirms core truths found in earlier scriptures and alludes to signs in those books predicting Muhammad’s prophethood, called glad tidings of prophethood in Islamic sources.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r8.anchor: Kur’an’ın önceki peygamberlere indirilenlerle aynı temel gerçekleri dile getirdiği hatırlatılmakta, aynı zamanda önceki kitaplarda Muhammed aleyhisselâmın geleceğini haber veren işaretlere ilişkin bir imada bulunulmaktadır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r2.claim: The Qur’an itself is the greatest sign and was sent to convey the truth conclusively.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r2.anchor: It has been sent to them so that

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r2.claim: When opponents were cornered in argument, they demanded a sign, meaning a miracle or the threatened punishment; People of the Book were especially responsible and encouraged idolaters to ask for what earlier messengers showed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r2.anchor: When the Prophet’s adversaries would feel helpless and cornered in countering him through arguments, as a last resort, they would demand from a sign of him being God’s envoy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r3.claim: The People of the Book are answered first: the advent of the last Messenger, predicted in their scriptures and confirming those prophecies, is already a sufficient sign.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r3.anchor: the last messenger whose advent was predicted in their scriptures

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r4.claim: The fulfillment of the scriptural prophecies about the last Messenger is the sign called bayyina in this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r4.anchor: the last messenger whose advent was predicted in their scriptures has now come

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r1.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, and Hafs read تأتهم with feminine agreement; the remaining readers use the masculine yā form because grammatical femininity is nonliteral.
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r1.anchor: بالتأنيث, والباقون بالياء من تحت؛ لأن التأنيث مجازي.

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r2.claim: The choice between feminine agreement and masculine yā reflects the feminine meaning of ما versus its grammatical form.
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r2.anchor: فحملا على معنى " ما " ، ومن قرأ بياء الغيبة فعلى لفظها.

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r3.claim: The general reading makes بيّنة a nominative construct with ما.
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r3.anchor: وقرأ العامة " بينة ما " بإضافة " بينة " إلى " ما " مرفوعة وهي واضحة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو فيما رواه أبو زيد
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r4.claim: In Abu Zayd's transmission, Abu Amr reads بيّنة with tanwin and nominative case; ما can then be an appositive or a predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو فيما رواه أبو زيد بتنوين " بينة " مرفوعة. وعلى هذه القراءة ففي " ما " أوجه،

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r5.claim: With that reading, ما may instead be a negative particle.

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r6.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r6.claim: The author of al-Lawami explains the negative reading as referring to abrogation and decisive rulings in the Quran that were absent from earlier books.
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r6.anchor: قال صاحب: اللوامح ": " وأريد بذلك ما في القرآن من الناسخ والفصل مما لم يكن

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r7.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r7.claim: A group reads بيّنة with tanwin and accusative; ما is then the subject and بيّنة a circumstantial accusative, feminine by sense.
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r7.anchor: وقرأت جماعة " بينة " بالتنوين والنصب. ووجهها أن تكون " ما " فاعلة، و " بينة " نصب

SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:20:133/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the ḥā of بيّنة without a vowel.

ASAD-NOTES:20:133/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:133/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:133/r1.claim: Truth-deniers demand a miracle from Muhammad, although clear evidence of the divine writ is already found in earlier scriptures.
ASAD-NOTES:20:133/r1.anchor: would but produce for us a miracle from his Sustainer! [119] [But] has there

ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n119/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n119/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n119/r1.claim: The demanded sign would prove Muhammad's prophetic mission; deniers often make belief in the Qur'an conditional on tangible miracles, as in 6:109.
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n119/r1.anchor: in proof of his prophetic mission: cf. 6:109 and, many other instances in which the deniers of the truth

ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r1.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether the Qur'an conveys the same fundamental truths as earlier prophetic revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r1.anchor: Does not the Qur'an express the same fundamental truths as were expressed in the revelations granted to the earlier prophets?

ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r2.claim: Asad also sees an allusion to earlier predictions of Muhammad, including Deuteronomy 18:15, 18 and Jesus' Comforter sayings; he discusses these at 2:42 and 61:6.
ASAD-NOTES:20:133#n120/r2.anchor: the above rhetorical question contains an allusion to the predictions of the advent of Muhammad to be found in the earlier scriptures

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p760/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p760/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p760/r4.claim: “Lawlā/lawmā” expresses impossibility when followed by a noun, but serves as a particle of exhortation or prompting when followed by a verb.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p760/r4.anchor: (لوما) إما أن تكون حرف امتناع لوجوب عندما تدخل على الأسماء أو تكون من حروف التخصيص عندما تدخل على الأفعال (لوما يأتينا بآية)

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r1.claim: Nafi, Abu Amr, and Hafs from Asim read the verb with feminine tāʾ: taʾtihim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r1.anchor: فقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم: أولم تأتهم بالتاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r2.speaker: الباقون وعاصم برواية أبي بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r2.claim: The other readers, including Asim in Abu Bakr's narration, read the verb with yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r3.claim: The tāʾ reading agrees with the feminine grammatical gender of bayyina; the yāʾ reading is allowed because bayyina and bayān are synonymous, as are mawʿiẓa/waʿẓ and ṣayḥa/ṣawt.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p253/r3.anchor: من قرأ: بالتاء فلتأنيث لفظة البينة، ومن قرأ بالياء فلأن البينة والبيان معناهما واحد

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r1.claim: Although the anomalous readings are not used in recitation, Ibn Jinnī considers them strong, divinely intended for acceptance and application, and beloved to God.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r1.anchor: فإنا نعتقد قوة هذا المسمى شاذا، وأنه مما أمر الله تعالى بتقبله، وأراد منا العمل بموجبه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r2.claim: A motive for the book was that predecessors had transmitted anomalous readings and sometimes explained individual forms, but had not produced a dedicated work arguing their cases as Ibn Jinnī wanted.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: لم يضعوا للحجاج كتابا فيه، ولا أولوه طرفان من القول عليه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: الشريف الرضي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r3.claim: Al-Sharif al-Raḍī reports that their teacher Abu al-Fath wrote a book arguing for anomalous readings late in his life.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: قال الشريف الرضي: كان شيخنا أبو الفتح النحوي عمل في آخر عمره كتابا يشتمل على الاحتجاج بقراءة الشواذ

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r4.claim: The author reads Ibn Jinnī’s afterlife-focused prayer as revealing his desire to prepare for the hereafter; the title al-Muḥtasab points to that purpose rather than the book’s subject.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: ولعله لذلك سماه المحتسب، واختار أن يدل باسمه على الغرض الذي يريده به، لا على الموضوع الذي يديره عليه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r5.claim: Al-Muḥtasab follows the method of al-Ḥujja, with differences required by the task of arguing for common and anomalous readings.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: ومنهج المحتسب كمنهج الحجة، لا يكاد يخالفه إلا بمقدار ما تقتضيه طبيعة الاحتجاج لقراءة الجماعة والقراءة الشاذة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r6.claim: For each reading Ibn Jinnī identifies its reciter and looks for linguistic witnesses, analogies, dialect support, or a suitable interpretation, explaining briefly or fully as needed.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p11#2/r6.anchor: يعرض القراءة، ويذكر من قرأ بها، ثم يرجع في أمرها إلى اللغة، يلتمس لها شاهدا فيرويه، أو نظيرا فيقيسها عليه

QIRAAT-ER:20:133:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:133:11#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:20:133:11#1/r1.claim: A masculine verb replaces feminine taʾtihim, either treating bayyina as semantically masculine or implying another subject.
QIRAAT-ER:20:133:11#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: Masculine verb replacing feminine taʾtihim — either treats bayyina as semantically masculine

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r1.claim: The deniers ask for a sign proving Muhammad’s prophethood or one of their proposed signs, discounting the miracles already shown to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r1.anchor: هلا يأتينا بآية تدل على صدقة في دعوى النبوة أو بآية من الآيات التي اقترحوها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r2.claim: Their obstinate rejection had reached the point that they no longer counted the witnessed miracles, which could make solid mountains tremble, as signs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r2.anchor: بلغوا من المكابرة والعناد إلى حيث لم يعدوا ما شاهدوا من المعجزات

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r3.claim: The reply identifies the requested proof as the Qur’an, the greatest and most beneficial miracle: its supreme knowledge appeared through someone who had neither studied nor practiced the sciences.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r3.anchor: القرآن الكريم الذي هو أم الآيات وأس المعجزات وأرفعها وأنفعها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r4.claim: The earlier scriptures are the Torah, Gospel, and other revealed books; their contents are true doctrines and foundational rulings shared by all messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r4.anchor: المراد بالصحف الأولى التوراة والانجيل وسائر الكتب السماوية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r5.claim: Calling the Qur’an a proof highlights its distinction and self-sufficient evidence; saying the proof itself came stresses its originality and suits the word bayyina.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r5.anchor: وفي إيراده بهذا العنوان ما لا يخفى من التنويه بشأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r6.claim: The hamza denies their claim and the waw joins an omitted premise: other signs came, and especially this proof came, making denial impossible despite their obstinacy.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r6.anchor: والهمزة لانكار الوقوع والواو للعطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r7.speaker: الإمام والطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r7.claim: Al-Imam and al-Tabarsi instead take the proof as Qur’anic accounts of earlier peoples destroyed after demanding and then rejecting signs; al-Alusi judges this interpretation unacceptable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r7.anchor: وزعم الأمام والطبرسي أن المعنى اولم ياتهم في القرإن بيان ما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r8.speaker: أكثر السبعة وأبو بحرية وابن محيصن وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وابن منذر وخلف وأبو عبيد وابن سعدان وابن عيسى وابن جبير الأنطاكي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r8.claim: These reciters read the verb in the proof clause with yāʾ, allowing masculine agreement because the feminine subject āya is separated from the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ اكثر السبعة وابو بحرية وابن محيصن وطلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r1.speaker: أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r1.claim: Abu Zayd’s report from Abu Amr reads bayyinatin with tanwīn and treats mā as its appositive substitute.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r1.anchor: أبو زيد عن أبي عمرو ( بينة ) بالتنوين على أن ما بدل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r2.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r2.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiḥ allows mā to be negative on this reading, referring to Qur’anic abrogating material and merit absent from previous books; al-Alusi dismisses this proposal.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r2.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح : يجوز أن تكون ما على هذه القراءة نافية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r3.speaker: فرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r3.claim: Another group reads bayyinatan with accusative and tanwīn, construing it as a circumstantial accusative and mā as the subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r3.anchor: بنصب ( بينة ) والتنوين على أنه حال وما فاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to read al-ṣuḥuf with a sukūn on ḥāʾ for ease of pronunciation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p286/r4.anchor: وقرأت فرقة منهم ابن عباس الصحف باسكان الحاء للتخفيف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r3.claim: After presenting ancient peoples' stories, answering Jewish challenges, and interweaving wisdom and admonition with a call to piety, the sūrah marvels that Quraysh still refuse truth through pride or fear of consequences.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r3.anchor: ما ذكر من قصص الأولين وأخبار الماضين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r4.claim: They demand a sign like those given to former peoples, from Muhammad, God's Messenger and beneficiary.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r4.anchor: أي محمد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r5.claim: The Qur'an's rulings and wisdom in unsurpassed meanings and arrangement already silence eloquent people and prove it is God's speech, though the opponents obstinately count none of these proofs as a sign.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r6.claim: The earlier scriptures include the books of Abraham, Moses, Jesus, David, the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and other divine books; the sūrah's accounts of Adam and Moses illustrate their contents.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r6.anchor: صحف إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى وداود عليهم السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r7.claim: The Qur'an recounts prior-scriptural events accurately in a form unknown to all but a few experts, without studying with them and without anyone able to match its arrangement; this establishes God as its sole teacher and messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r7.anchor: من غير أن يخالط عالما منهم أو من غيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r8.claim: The Qur'an itself witnesses to prior scriptures, as a proof bears witness for what is proved; it needs no witness and surpasses all the signs requested of earlier prophets by an immeasurable degree.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p60/r8.anchor: لا افتقار له بعد العجز عنه إلى شيء أصلا

BURSEVI:v5p345/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r1.claim: The speakers are the Quraysh disbelievers, demanding a sign of the kind they and their associates proposed, such as those given to Moses and Jesus.

BURSEVI:v5p345/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r2.claim: Their stubbornness reached the point that they refused to count the miracles they had already witnessed as signs.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r2.anchor: بلغوا من العناد إلى حيث لم يعدوا ما شاهدوا من المعجزات من قبيل الآيات

BURSEVI:v5p345/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r3.claim: The hamza denies that the proof failed to arrive; the waw joins the question to an omitted preceding clause, and bayyina means a clear rational or sensory indication.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r3.anchor: الهمزة لإنكار الوقوع والواو للعطف على مقدر والبينة الدلالة الواضحة عقلية كانت أو حسية

BURSEVI:v5p345/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r4.claim: Suhuf is the plural of sahifa, a written page; the author says the alphabet letters are separate pages among what was sent down to Adam.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r4.anchor: والصحف جمع صحيفة وهي التي يكتب فيها وحروف التهجي صحيفة على حدة مما أنزل على آدم

BURSEVI:v5p345/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r5.claim: The earlier pages refer to the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and the other revealed books.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r5.anchor: والمراد بها التوراة والإنجيل والزبور وسائر الكتب السماوية

BURSEVI:v5p345/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r6.claim: The proof is the Qur'an, which explains for people the true doctrines and foundational rulings shared by all messengers; it is the greatest sign of all.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r6.anchor: القرآن الذي فيه بيان للناس وما عبارة عن العقائد الحقية وأصول الأحكام التي اجتمعت عليها كافة الرسل

BURSEVI:v5p345/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r7.claim: The Qur'an contains the essence of earlier revelation, verifies its truth and its accounts of past nations, and is itself an inimitable proof that can establish the truth of the other books.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r7.anchor: وهو شاهد بحقية ما فيها وبصحة ما ينطق به من أنباء الأمم من حيث أنه غني بإعجازه عما يشهد بحقيته

BURSEVI:v5p345/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r8.claim: Its inclusion of the earlier books' core teachings, despite its bearer being unlettered and never studying them, makes its miraculous character clear.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r8.anchor: اشتماله على زبدة ما فيها مع أن الآتي به أمي لم يرها ولم يتعلم ممن علمها إعجاز بين

BURSEVI:v5p345/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p345/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p345/r9.claim: The Qur'anic proof leaves no excuse for abandoning the revealed laws and following the path of error, a point the next verse develops.
BURSEVI:v5p345/r9.anchor: ثم بين أنه لا عذر لهم في ترك الشرائع وسلوك طريق الضلالة بوجه ما فقال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r1.claim: Messengers came with signs open to reflection and supported by rational proofs; those foreknown to stray stray, while those foreknown to guidance are guided.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r1.anchor: ورسل الله إنما اقترنت معهم آيات معرضة للنظر محفوفة بالبراهين العقلية ليضل من سبق في علم الله تعالى ضلاله ويهتدي من سبق في علم الله تعالى هداه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r2.claim: The rebuke points to the Torah as the greatest witness and sign for Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r2.anchor: يعني التوراة أعظم شاهد وأكبر آية له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r3.claim: These readers make the verb agree with feminine بينة.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم «تأتهم» على لفظة بينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r4.speaker: الباقون وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r4.claim: The remaining readers use masculine agreement by sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وأبو بكر عن عاصم «يأتهم» بالياء على المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r5.claim: A group reads بينة ما as a construct phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r5.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «بينة ما» بالإضافة إلى ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r6.claim: Another group gives بينة tanwin and makes ما the subject of تأتي.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «بينة» بالتنوين، وما على هذه القراءة فاعلة ب «تأتي»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r7.claim: The majority read the ḥāʾ in الصحف with ḍamma.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p71/r8.claim: A group reads the ḥāʾ in الصحف with sukūn.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r1.claim: The speakers are the polytheists, asking why Muhammad does not bring a sign from God like the signs given to earlier prophets, such as the she-camel or staff.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وقالوا يعني المشركين لولا أي هلا يأتينا محمد بآية من ربه أي كآيات الأنبياء نحو الناقة والعصا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r2.claim: Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, and Hafs from ʿAsim read the verb with tāʾ, addressing the feminine subject.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r2.anchor: قرأ نافع وابو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم تأتهم بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read the verb with yāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم يأتهم بالياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r4.claim: The Qur'an contains a clear explanation, and earlier scriptures contain accounts of nations destroyed after demanding signs and then rejecting them; the current questioners may meet the same fate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p336/r4.anchor: أي أولم يأتهم في القرآن بيان وما في الكتب من أخبار الأمم التي أهلكناها لما سألوا الآيات ثم كفروا بها فما يؤمنهم أن تكون حالهم في سؤال الآيات كحال أولئك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r1.claim: The disbelievers ask why Muhammad does not bring a sign from his Lord, meaning a mark that proves he is God's messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r1.anchor: بعلامة دالة على صدقه في أنه رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r2.claim: The proof is the revealed Quran: Muhammad was unlettered, had not studied with the People of the Book, yet it tells earlier histories in agreement with authentic prior scriptures, confirms what is true, and exposes their false additions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r2.anchor: يعني: القرآن العظيم الذي أنزله عليه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r3.claim: The argument parallels 29:50–51: the Quran recited to them should suffice as a mercy and reminder for believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية كقوله تعالى في سورة "العنكبوت"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r4.claim: The Prophet said every prophet received signs like those that led people to believe, while his own gift was revelation from God, and he hoped for the largest following on Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r4.anchor: وفي الصحيح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the Quran as Muhammad's greatest sign and says he had countless other miracles, documented elsewhere in the books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p329/r5.anchor: وإنما ذكر هاهنا أعظم الآيات التي أعطيها، عليه السلام، وهو القرآن

MUJAHID:v1p406/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p406/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p406/r1.claim: The clear proof in the earlier scriptures means the Torah and Gospel.
MUJAHID:v1p406/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ بينة ما في الصحف الأولى ﴾ قال يعني التوراة والإنجيل

MUQATIL:20:133-135/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r1.claim: The speakers are Meccan unbelievers asking for a sign to show Muhammad is a prophet and messenger, as signs came to earlier prophets and their peoples.
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r1.anchor: { وقالوا } أى كفار مكة: { لولا } يعنى هلا { يأتينا بآية من ربه

MUQATIL:20:133-135/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r2.claim: The clear proof is the explanation in the books of Abraham and Moses, which preceded Muhammad's book.
MUQATIL:20:133-135/r2.anchor: { أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى } [آية: 133] يعنى بيان كتب إبراهيم وموسى

MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r6.claim: Muqatil derives Adam's name from the earth's surface, Hawwa's from a living being, Noah's from lamenting, and Abraham's from being father of nations or a merciful father.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل: تفسير آدم، عليه السلام، لأنه خلق من أديم الأرض، وتفسير حواء

MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r7.claim: Muqatil explains Isaac's name by Sarah's laughter, Jacob's by grasping Esau's heel in the womb, and Joseph's as an increase in beauty.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r7.anchor: وتفسير إسحاق لضحك سارة، ويعقوب لأنه خرج من بطن أمه قابض على عقب العيص

MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r8.claim: Muqatil explains Yahya's name as revived or brought to life between two elderly parents, a very old man and a barren woman.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#3/r8.anchor: وتفسير يحيى: أحيى من بين ميتين، لأنه خرج من بين شيخ كبير، وعجوز عاقر

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r1.claim: In a dream, Gabriel told the Prophet that God granted him his whole community on Judgment Day and would grant others if he asked; the Prophet rejoiced.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r1.anchor: دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r2.claim: In another dream, Gabriel told the Prophet that Paradise longed for him and his community, which made him laugh joyfully.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r2.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، بينما هو نائم إذ ضحك

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r3.claim: In a third dream the Prophet saw his community carrying rods of light that illuminated the distance between east and west; Gabriel identified them as Islam.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r3.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، بينما هو نائم إذ ضحك

MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r4.claim: The Prophet saw Paradise's pearl and ruby palaces and was told they were for him and his community, adorned two thousand years before his creation.
MUQATIL:20:133-135#4/r4.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ابنة عمته أم هانىء فنعس، فوضعت له وسادة، فوضع رأسه فنام، بينما هو نائم إذ ضحك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r1.claim: The speakers are disbelievers demanding that Muhammad bring a sign from his Lord to prove his prophethood.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r1.anchor: ﴾ أي الكافرون ﴿ لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r2.claim: Madani, Hafs, and Basri read “has it not come to them”; other readers read “have they not come to them.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r2.anchor: / أو لم يأتهم / أو لم تأتهم مدني وحفص وبصري

NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r3.claim: In reply to their obstinate demand, the Quran itself is presented as the clearest sign and greatest miracle: it verifies earlier revealed books, which depend on its testimony because they are not miracles themselves.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p73/r3.anchor: يعني أنهم اقترحوا على عادتهم في التعنت آية على النبوة فقيل لهم أو لم أنكم آية هي أم الآيات

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r1.claim: The Meccan unbelievers demanded a sign from Muhammad that compelled certain knowledge, a manifest sign like the she-camel or staff, or the specific signs they requested as earlier peoples had.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r1.anchor: يريد كفار مكة أي لولا يأتينا محمد بآية توجب العلم الضروري. أو بآية ظاهرة كالناقة والعصا.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r2.claim: The earlier scriptures—the Torah, Gospel, and prior books—are themselves a greater sign because Muhammad reported their contents.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r2.anchor: يريد التوراة والإنجيل والكتب المتقدمة، وذلك أعظم آية إذ أخبر بما فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r3.claim: A variant lightens the pronunciation of الصحف.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the proof as the prophecies of Muhammad found in earlier scriptures, which attest his prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r4.anchor: وقيل: أولم تأتهم الآية الدالة على نبوته بما وجدوه في الكتب المتقدمة من البشارة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r5.claim: Another view says the proof is God's destruction of earlier peoples who rejected and demanded signs; the Meccans might suffer the same fate if signs came.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r5.anchor: وقيل: أولم يأتهم إهلاكنا الأمم الذين كفروا واقترحوا الآيات فما يؤمنهم إن أتتهم الآيات

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق وحفص
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Yaʿqub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read تأتهم with feminine ت to agree with البينة.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وابن أبي إسحاق وحفص «أولم تأتهم» بالتاء لتأنيث البينة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r7.speaker: الباقون وأبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r7.claim: The remaining readers use ي, reflecting the earlier verb position or treating البينة as البيان والبرهان; Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim prefer this reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r7.anchor: الباقون بالياء لتقدم الفعل ولأن البينة هي البيان والبرهان فردوه إلى المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r8.speaker: الكسائي والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r8.claim: Al-Kisaʾi transmits the construction; al-Nahhas says if بينة is indefinite and nominative, ما is its apposition, while if accusative it is circumstantial, meaning the earlier-scripture content came manifestly.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:133-134/r8.anchor: وحكى الكسائي «أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى» قال: ويجوز على هذا «بينة ما في الصحف الأولى». قال النحاس: إذا نونت «بينة» ورفعت جعلت «ما» بدلا

STUDYQURAN:20:133/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r1.claim: The Makkans repeatedly demanded that the Prophet bring a sign.
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r1.anchor: The Makkans made repeated requests for the Prophet to bring them a sign

STUDYQURAN:20:133/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r2.claim: The clear proof may refer to Quranic stories also found in earlier scriptures, which demonstrate the Quran's divine source.
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r2.anchor: The clear proof of that which is in the scriptures of old is a reference to the various stories in the Quran that are also found in the previous scriptures

STUDYQURAN:20:133/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r3.claim: Alternatively, it may refer to Torah and Gospel passages that mention Muhammad.
STUDYQURAN:20:133/r3.anchor: Alternatively, this part of the verse can be a reference to those parts of the Torah and the Gospel that mention the Prophet Muhammad

TAB-FULL:v16p218/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r1.claim: The polytheists ask for a sign like Ṣāliḥ's she-camel or Jesus's miracles; al-Ṭabarī answers that earlier scriptures already show how peoples who demanded signs then disbelieved were destroyed.
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r1.anchor: بيان ما في الكتب التي قبل هذا الكتاب من أنباء الأمم من قبلهم التي أهلكناهم لما سألوا الآيات فكفروا بها لما أتتهم كيف عجلنا لهم العذاب

TAB-FULL:v16p218/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r2.claim: Earlier scriptures already tell how nations were destroyed after demanding signs and then disbelieving; a new sign might likewise bring them swift punishment rather than belief.
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r2.anchor: بيان ما في الكتب التي قبل هذا الكتاب من أنباء الأمم من قبلهم التي أهلكناهم لما سألوا الآيات فكفروا بها لما أتتهم كيف عجلنا لهم العذاب

TAB-FULL:v16p218/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the earlier scriptures as the Torah and Gospel.
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى} [طه: 133] قال: التوراة والإنجيل

TAB-FULL:v16p218/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r4.claim: Qatāda says the proof is the books of earlier peoples whose former settlements the Meccans pass through.
TAB-FULL:v16p218/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أولم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى} [طه: 133] الكتب التي خلت من الأمم التي يمشون في مساكنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r2.claim: They demand that Muḥammad bring a sign from his Lord like those given to earlier prophets, such as the she-camel or the staff.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r2.anchor: هلا يأتينا محمد بآية من ربه كما أتى بها الأنبياء نحو الناقة والعصا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says signs had already come to them, but they demanded signs of their own choosing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (وقد أتتهم الآيات ولكنهم طلبوا أن يأتيهم ما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r4.claim: The Qurʾān clarifies the Torah, Gospel, and earlier scriptures and is a greater sign, since an unlettered Prophet reported their contents without reading them, as the People of the Book attest; this is al-Kalbī's view and that of others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r4.anchor: وذلك أعظم آية إذ أخبر أمي بما فيها من غير قراءة كتاب على ما تصدقه أهل الكتب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r5.speaker: قول آخر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r5.claim: Another view says the Qurʾān warns through accounts of earlier peoples destroyed after demanding and rejecting signs, raising the question why these people would respond differently.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r5.anchor: وفيه قول آخر وهو: (أن المعنى أولم تأتهم ببيان ما في الكتب من أنباء الأمم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r6.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r6.claim: Some exegetes understand the proof in the earlier scriptures as their glad tidings of Muḥammad and descriptions of his qualities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التفسير: {بينة ما في الصحف الأولى} ما تقدم من البشارة بمحمد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r1.claim: The clear proof in the earlier scriptures is the Torah and Gospel, as in 7:157, which says the unlettered Prophet is written about there.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r1.anchor:
التوراة والإنجيل كقوله: {النبي الأمي الذي يجدونه مكتوبا عندهم في التوراة
والإنجيل} [الأعراف: 157] .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the earlier scriptures as the Torah and Gospel.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r3.claim: Qatadah says the phrase refers to the books that came before; Yahya notes the two explanations amount to one.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295#2/r3.anchor:
وقال قتادة: الكتب قبله.
وهو واحد.

BURHAN:v1p311/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p311/r1.claim: Recognizing the most eloquent wording and construction is a major Qur'anic science for interpreters: they must preserve the demands of inimitability, truth and metaphor, composition, fit with the passage's purpose, and freedom from discord.
BURHAN:v1p311/r1.anchor: وهذا العلم أعظم أركان المفسر فإنه لا بد من مراعاة ما يقتضية الإعجاز من الحقيقة والمجاز وتأليف النظم

BURHAN:v1p311/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p311/r2.claim: The author cites Ibn al-Naqib's two-volume work and Hazim al-Andalusi's Minhaj al-Bulagha among the comprehensive treatments, and says al-Kashshaf is especially rich in this science.
BURHAN:v1p311/r2.anchor: وأجمعها ما جمعه الشيخ شمس الدين محمد بن النقيب مجلدين قدمهما أمام تفسيره وما وضعه حازم الأندلسي المسمى بمنهاج البلغاء

BURHAN:v1p311/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r3.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v1p311/r3.claim: Al-Sakkaki says inimitability is perceived but cannot be described, like metrical correctness or charm; sound innate ability develops it through mastery and practice of semantics and rhetoric.
BURHAN:v1p311/r3.anchor: قال السكاكي واعلم أن شأن الإعجاز عجيب يدرك ولا يمكن وصفه كاستقامة الوزن تدرك ولا يمكن وصفها

BURHAN:v1p311/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v1p311/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says an interpreter must preserve the Qur'an's beautiful ordering, complete eloquence and unspoiled challenge; without command of Arabic usage, one falls far short.
BURHAN:v1p311/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى من حق مفسر كتاب الله الباهر وكلامه المعجز أن يتعاهد فى مذاهبه بقاء النظم على حسنه

BURHAN:v1p311/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r5.speaker: أبو الطيب
BURHAN:v1p311/r5.claim: Abu al-Tayyib argues that many features of this science are not Qur'anic rhetoric because he holds that the Qur'an was revealed contrary to the Arabs' styles; the author says this will be discussed later.
BURHAN:v1p311/r5.anchor: وادعى القاضى أبو الطيب فى كتاب إعجاز القرآن أن كثيرا من محاسن هذا العلم لا يعد من البلاغة القرآنية

BURHAN:v1p311/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p311/r6.claim: The early generations did not discuss rhetoric because revelation aimed to teach law, Islamic ordinances and faith, while eloquence functioned as a miracle rather than a subject for instruction.
BURHAN:v1p311/r6.anchor: قلت إنما سكت الأولون عنه لأن القصد من إنزال القرآن تعليم الحلال والحرام وتعريف شرائع الإسلام وقواعد الإيمان

BURHAN:v1p311/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p311/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p311/r7.claim: The Qur'an's particular eloquence was not itself the intended teaching, and the early scholars already knew Arabic rhetorical styles; unlike legal derivation, that knowledge did not need explanation.
BURHAN:v1p311/r7.anchor: وإنما جاءت لتكون معجزة وما قصد به الإعجاز لا سبيل إلى معرفة طريقه فلم يكن الخوض فيه مسوغا

NAHHAS:v3p59/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p59/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p59/r18.claim: If بينة is nominative with tanwīn, ما is apposition; if بينة is accusative, it is circumstantial, meaning the earlier scriptures came clearly.
NAHHAS:v3p59/r18.anchor: قال أبو جعفر إذا نونت بينة ورفعت جعلت ما بدلا منها وإذا نصبتها على الحال والمعنى أو لم يأتهم ما في الصحف الأولى مبينا

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r16.claim: The opponents' demand for a sign insinuates that they are being asked to believe without one; elsewhere they call the revelation confused dreams.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r16.anchor: أوهموا بهذا الكلام أنه يكلفهم الإيمان من غير آية

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r17.claim: One explanation is that the Quran's agreement with earlier scriptures, though Muhammad had no schooling or teacher, conveyed unseen knowledge and was itself a miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r17.anchor: أن ما في القرآن إذ وافق ما في كتبهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r18.claim: A second explanation is that the earlier scriptures contain prophecies of Muhammad, his prophethood, and his mission.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r18.anchor: أن بينة ما في الصحف الأولى ما فيها من البشارة بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبنبوته وبعثته

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r19.speaker: ابن جرير والقفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r19.claim: Ibn Jarīr and al-Qaffāl say the proof is the Quran's account of earlier peoples destroyed after demanding signs and disbelieving, a warning that these questioners might meet the same fate.

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r20.claim: The masculine pronoun referring back to the feminine “bayyina” is justified because “bayyina” has the masculine sense of proof or evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r20.anchor: واعلم أنه إنما ذكر الضمير الراجع إلى البينة لأنها في معنى البرهان والدليل

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r5.claim: The Meccan polytheists taunt the Prophet by demanding another miracle, implying that the Qur'an does not prove his prophethood.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r5.anchor: حكاية قول مشركي مكة وإنما قالوا هذا تعريضا للقرآن أنه ليس بآية دالة على النبوة

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r6.claim: Bayyina can mean an evidencing witness or clear proof; another reported sense is explanatory clarification.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r6.anchor: والبينة الشاهد المبين أو البين وقيل هو البيان

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r7.claim: On the first sense of bayyina, the Qur'an witnesses to and clarifies truths in the Torah, Gospel, and other scriptures, despite the Prophet having no teacher.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r7.anchor: على الوجه الأول من معنيي البينة أو لم تأتهم بينة وشاهد يشهد

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r8.claim: On the second sense, the Qur'an recounts earlier peoples who demanded signs, received them, then were destroyed for disbelieving; this should end demands for further signs.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r8.anchor: وعلى الوجه الثاني أو لم يأتهم بيان ما في الصحف من أخبار الأمم الماضين

TABRISI:20:131/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:131/r2.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وقتيبة وحفص
TABRISI:20:131/r2.claim: The people of Medina and Basra, Qutayba, and Hafs read تأتهم with tāʾ; the other readers read it with yāʾ.
TABRISI:20:131/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة وقتيبة وحفص أو لم تأتهم بالتاء والباقون بالياء

TABRISI:20:132-135/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r11.claim: The disbelievers demand a sign of their choosing from Muhammad, such as the she-camel given to earlier prophets.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r11.anchor: اقترحناها عليه كما أتى به الأنبياء، نحو الناقة

TABRISI:20:132-135/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r12.claim: The Qur’an explains what earlier scriptures relate about peoples destroyed after they demanded signs and then disbelieved; the Meccans have no assurance their fate would differ.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r12.anchor: أي أو لم يأتهم في القرآن بيان ما في الكتب الأولى من أنباء الأمم التي أهلكناهم لما اقترحوا الآيات ثم كفروا بها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r6.claim: The speakers are the polytheists, who ask Muhammad for the signs they proposed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r6.anchor: يعني: المشركين { لولا } هلا { يأتينا } محمد عليه السلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r7.claim: The proof from earlier scriptures is the Qur'an, which explains what is in the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r7.anchor: { ما في الصحف الأولى } يعني: في القرآن بيان ما في التوراة والإنجيل والزبور

QASHANI:20:131-133/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:131-133/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:131-133/r6.claim: The earlier scriptures contain certain truths, wisdoms, and knowledge fixed in heavenly tablets and upper spirits.
QASHANI:20:131-133/r6.anchor: { أو لم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى } من الحقائق والحكم والمعارف اليقينية الثابتة في الألواح السماوية

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r15.claim: Those who demanded proof were blind in insight; the failure lay in their perception, not in the evidence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r15.anchor: عميت بصائرهم وادعوا أنه لا برهان معه ، ولم يكن القصور في الأدلة بل كان الخلل في بصائرهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r16.claim: Even every sign they requested would only increase their tyranny, disbelief, and loss if God did not will them to believe.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r16.anchor: ولو جمع الله لهم كل آية اقترحت على رسول ثم لم يرد } الله أن يؤمنوا لما ازدادوا إلا طغيانا وكفرا وخسرانا

ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r5.claim: Their request means why does he not bring a sign; signs had already come, but they wanted to prescribe which signs would support them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p380#2/r5.anchor: معناه هلا يأتينا بآية أمن ربه

NASHR:v2p322/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r4.speaker: نافع والبصريان وابن جماز وحفص وابن وردان
NASHR:v2p322/r4.claim: Nafi, the two Basrans, Ibn Jammaz, and Hafs read أولم تأتهم with feminine tāʾ. Ibn Wardan's transmitters differ: some give feminine tāʾ, others masculine yāʾ; the rest use yāʾ.
NASHR:v2p322/r4.anchor: فقرأ نافع، والبصريان، وابن جماز وحفص بالتاء على التأنيث،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r8.claim: The unbelievers ask for a proposed sign, although the Prophet had already brought many signs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r8.anchor: {وقالوا} يعني المشركين، {لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r9.speaker: أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص عن عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r9.claim: Medina and Basra readers and Ḥafṣ read taʾtihim, feminine to agree with bayyinah; the others read yaʾtihim, with the verb preceding and agreeing semantically with “clarification.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r9.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والبصرة وحفص عن عاصم: " تأتهم " لتأنيث البينة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r10.claim: One explanation is that the Qur’an clarifies the earlier scriptures and is stronger in proof and clearer as a sign.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r10.anchor: أي بيان ما فيها، وهو القرآن أقوى دلالة وأوضح آية.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r11.claim: Another explanation is that earlier scriptures recount nations who requested signs but did not believe when signs came; the Meccans may fare likewise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r11.anchor: التوراة، والإنجيل، وغيرهما من أنباء الأمم أنهم اقترحوا الآيات، فلما أتتهم ولم يؤمنوا بها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r7.claim: They may demand a sign proving his prophethood or a sign they propose, rejecting existing signs out of stubbornness and hostility.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r7.anchor: بآية تدل على صدقه في إهداء النبوة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r8.claim: The Qur'an answers them as the mother of miracles, greatest and most enduring, because knowledge outranks action in status and lasting effect, and a prophetic miracle is extraordinary knowledge or action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r8.anchor: فألزمهم بإتيانه بالقرآن الذي هو أم المعجزات وأعظمها وأبقاها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r9.claim: The earlier scriptures include the Torah, Gospel, and other revealed books. Their essentials of belief and universal law appear in the Qur'an brought by an unlettered man who had not studied them, a clear miracle; earlier books require proof of authenticity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r9.anchor: من التوراة والإنجيل وسائر الكتب السماوية

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r10.claim: الصحف is also read with a light consonant; Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read تأتهم with تاء, while the other readers use ياء.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r10.anchor: وقرىء »الصحف« بالتخفيف وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the earlier scriptures meant by the proof are the Torah and Gospel.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {أو لم تأتهم بينة ما في الصحف الأولى} قال: التوراة والإنجيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r21.claim: Groups of disbelievers demanded a proposed sign from Muḥammad, one that would overwhelm and compel them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r21.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى عن طوائف من الكفار قالوا عن محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، لولا يأتينا بآية من ربه أي بعلامة مما اقترحناها عليه

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r32.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r32.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r32.claim: The disbelievers ask Muhammad for a proof of prophethood from his Lord, like those given to earlier prophets.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r32.anchor: وقالوا يعني الكفار لولا يأتينا محمد بآية من ربه أي: بحجة تدل على نبوته عن عند ربه

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r33.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r33.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r33.claim: One explanation says they had dictated which signs they wanted, yet did not believe when those signs came, and were destroyed.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r33.anchor: قيل: تحكموا في طلب الآيات، فلما جاءتهم لم يؤمنوا، فعذبوا بالاستئصال، وقيل:

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r34.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r34.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r34.claim: The first scriptures contain glad tidings in the Torah and Gospel that match the Prophet's description.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r34.anchor: وقيل: ما في التوراة والإنجيل من البشارة بما وافق صفته - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r35.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r35.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r35.claim: Abu Muslim reads the proof as the Qur'an's explanation of what is in earlier scriptures; the Prophet could know it only through revelation because he was unlettered.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r35.anchor: ولم يكن له طريق إليه إلا بالوحي

JISHUMI:v7p4774/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r3.claim: These verses establish the obligation of divine لطف: sending messengers removes people's excuse, whereas without a messenger they would have an argument against God.
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وقالوا لولا يأتينا) وقوله: (ولو أنا أهلكناهم) على وجوب اللطف؛ لأنه بين أنه بعث الرسول لطفا لهم

JISHUMI:v7p4774/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r5.claim: First anti-determinist argument: if no messenger had been sent, people would have an excuse; the determinist account makes messengers and admonitions useless and leaves an even stronger excuse.
JISHUMI:v7p4774/r5.anchor: لو لم يبعث رسولا لكان لهم الحجة
